# Claude Code — plugin enablement (read by `/b6p-setup` step 1)

Applies when `/b6p-setup` runs inside Claude Code (CLI or desktop app). Check first, act only on what is missing.


Two scopes:

- **Once per machine (`/b6p-setup` step 1):** the plugin is installed at **user scope** — `claude plugin marketplace add Bluestep-Systems/bluestep-ai`, then `claude plugin install bluestep-tools@bluestep` (the first prompt in the bluestep-ai README does both; internal staff usually get both through managed settings). If `/b6p-setup` is running, that part is already done on this tool; confirm the marketplace is registered with `claude plugin marketplace list` so updates arrive. A user-scope install loads the B6P skills, hooks and gateway MCP in **every** session on the machine, B6P project or not. That is what lets `/b6p-setup` run in a new, empty folder, but say the cost out loud: the guardrail hook fires in every repo, so an edit to any path containing `declarations/` is **blocked in any project on the machine**. Give the off switch with it: in a non-BlueStep repo, add `"enabledPlugins": { "bluestep-tools@bluestep": false }` to that project's `.claude/settings.json` — project settings override the user-scope entry, and the plugin stays installed for everything else. `/b6p-setup` writes that line for you when it is run in a repo that is not a B6P workspace.
- **Per project (`/b6p-setup` step 2):** writes the project's `.claude/settings.json` with the marketplace registration (`extraKnownMarketplaces`), the compaction window and the permission allowlist — **not** `enabledPlugins`: the install above is what enables the plugin, for every project on the machine, and a project-level `true` with no user-scope install does not load anything. When a teammate clones and trusts the folder, Claude Code registers the marketplace from it, so their one `claude plugin install bluestep-tools@bluestep --scope user` finds it. It does not replace the install above.

**Marketplace registration (read only).** Read `~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json` and `extraKnownMarketplaces` in `~/.claude/settings.json`, and find the `bluestep` entry. Never write either file. The entry names the old repo if its source is `github` with `repo` = `Bluestep-Systems/bspecs`, or `git` with a `url` on `github.com` whose repo path is `Bluestep-Systems/bspecs` (`https://`, `ssh://git@` or `git@github.com:` form, with or without `.git` or a trailing `/`, any case; `bspecs-something` is another repo). If either file names the old repo, put one note under the report's notes, never under what the machine still lacks: nothing is needed, updates follow the repo's rename. Offer the move below only when `~/.claude/settings.json` itself has the `bluestep` entry; otherwise (the marketplace came from managed settings or a project) say the organization's admin moves it, and suggest nothing. To move anyway, do **both** steps together — change the `bluestep` source in `~/.claude/settings.json` to `{ "source": "github", "repo": "Bluestep-Systems/bluestep-ai" }`, then run `claude plugin marketplace add Bluestep-Systems/bluestep-ai` — because either step alone stops the plugins loading. If the `add` is refused because a managed entry still names the old repo, put `~/.claude/settings.json` back as it was and leave it to the admin. Never suggest `claude plugin marketplace remove`: it uninstalls the plugins and deletes their data. The desktop app's Code tab uses the same two files, so the same check applies there.

**phi-guard (opt-in).** A separate plugin from the same marketplace: it blocks an agent's Edit or Write that looks like real client data. It is installed per machine (user scope), acts only in a B6P project (a `U######/` folder or the `AGENTS.md` marker `/b6p-setup` writes), and is turned off for one project with `"enabledPlugins": { "phi-guard@bluestep": false }` in that project's `.claude/settings.json`. Check read-only: on the CLI, `claude plugin list` shows `phi-guard@bluestep` when it is installed; on the desktop app, ask the user to look under Customize → Plugins. Missing → offer it, and on a yes hand over the install, do not run it: CLI `claude plugin install phi-guard@bluestep --scope user`; desktop app Customize → Plugins → Browse plugins → `phi-guard` → Install (plugins there are managed by the account, so the CLI command does not apply). The git client-data check `/b6p-setup` sets up in step 2 runs with or without it.

Plugin-bundled surfaces (MCP servers, hooks) load at session start: after enabling, use a fresh session or `/reload-plugins`.

**Desktop-app note.** Plugin-bundled MCP is account-managed via claude.ai, not local config, so desktop-app users may need to add the gateway **once** as a claude.ai custom connector (URL `https://gateway.bluestep.net/mcp`, Authorization `Bearer <b6pt_ token>`) rather than relying on the bundle. That is one gateway connector — **not** one per org.
